questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Get ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert drivers that a train might be near. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly, at an intersection, on a hill or curve, near a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What should you do before driving after taking medicine?

options.text: Ask your doctor if the medicine affects your driving ability.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if the medicine affects your driving ability.
questions.explanation: Many medicines can affect your ability to drive safely. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about any medicine before you drive. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes so you don't get hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas of your vision that blur when you are tired.
Road areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These hidden areas are called 'blind spots' because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning lights, or flaggers indicate a train is near. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if pedestrians are not using their phones.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian or vehicle already in the intersection pass. You may proceed carefully only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: There are no vehicles behind you.
You are listening to the radio.

questions.explanation: Leave extra space when following a motorcycle. This gives you room to stop safely if the motorcycle rider falls or stops suddenly.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass many cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will arrive much faster and safer.
You will increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass another vehicle, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: What happens to drivers who eat and drink while driving?

options.text: They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. This makes it hard to control your vehicle and stay in your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and will soon drive on a two-way highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that roadwork is coming. Watch for temporary traffic control devices when you enter a work zone.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your thinking and makes crashes more likely. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should continue driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.explanation: All vehicles must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead has its red lights flashing, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mean the bus is loading or unloading students. Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing before going. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving abilities.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.
Yes, it is a distracting activity.
No, it is not a distracting activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest thing to do is get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: Night driving presents unique problems because:

options.text: The speed limit is increased at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights reach. This makes it hard to judge how far away other cars are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are areas marked with white lines where pedestrians can cross the road safely. Some crosswalks are unmarked.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
questions.explanation: Your tires grip the road less when it is wet, snowy, or icy. You should slow down in these conditions.

questions.question: Seat belts are most effective when they are worn by:

options.text: Passengers when they are on a long drive.
All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.
All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object that can injure others.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, pull over at a rest stop to nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a full stop and wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear before you go.
